Three choices sit behind every fit: the engine, the estimator and the optimizer.
This page takes them in that order. The engine decides which models and effects
exist. The estimator decides what is minimized. The optimizer only searches for
the minimum. The formulas are in [Methods and Formulas](methods.html).

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Use this when:** you are choosing between the `glm`, `regmedint`, `lmer` and `sem` engines, or want to know what an estimator and an optimizer are.\
**You get:** a table of the engines with the page for each, and the meaning of estimator and optimizer.\
**Reading time:** 3 min
:::

## Engine

An engine is the fitter: it decides which models can be written and which
effects come out. medfit names an engine for the model family it fits or the
package that fits it.

| Engine | Fits | Use it for | Page |
|---|---|---|---|
| `"glm"` (default) | `stats::glm()` for the mediator and outcome models | formulas, any `glm` family, case weights | [Simple mediation](model-simple.html) |
| `"regmedint"` | closed-form natural effects from the regmedint package | VanderWeele's regression closed forms | [The regmedint engine](model-regmedint.html) |
| `"lmer"` | REML mixed models with a random cluster intercept | a treatment assigned to clusters (2-1-1) | [Cluster-level treatment](model-cluster.html) |
| `"sem"` | the sem engine: medfit's own maximum-likelihood SEM fitter | model syntax, latent mediators, constraints, `mbco_sem()` | [The sem engine](model-sem.html) |

The sem engine is reached in two ways: `fit_sem(model, data)`, which returns a
`SEMFit` for `extract_mediation()`, and `fit_mediation(engine = "sem", model = )`
for one mediator. `engine = "native"` is the earlier spelling of the same engine
and gives the same fit.

::: {.callout-note}
## The sem engine is not `lavaan::sem()`
"sem" names medfit's own fitter. A model fitted by `lavaan::sem()` reaches
medfit through `extract_mediation()` on the lavaan fit. That is an extraction
route, not an engine: lavaan does the fitting and medfit reads the paths. See
[lavaan fits](model-lavaan.html) and
[lavaan and the sem engine](lavaan-comparison.html).
:::

The engines do not return interchangeable numbers. The
[engines compared](models.html) table lists what each one estimates, which
families it takes and which standard errors it offers.

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
library(medfit)
```

The two spellings give the same fit:

```{r}
#| label: sem-alias
syntax <- "
  mediator1 ~ a * treatment + covariate1 + covariate2
  outcome ~ b * mediator1 + cp * treatment + covariate1 + covariate2
"
by_sem <- fit_mediation(model = syntax, data = mediation_demo,
                        treatment = "treatment", mediator = "mediator1",
                        engine = "sem")
by_native <- fit_mediation(model = syntax, data = mediation_demo,
                           treatment = "treatment", mediator = "mediator1",
                           engine = "native")
all.equal(coef(by_sem), coef(by_native))
```

## Estimator

The estimator is what the engine minimizes. Within the sem engine, the
`missing` argument switches between two estimators:

- `missing = "listwise"` (default): maximum likelihood on the complete rows.
- `missing = "fiml"`: bounded full-information maximum likelihood, which keeps
  rows with some values missing. It covers a small set of models, is
  numerically verified and is not statistically admitted. See
  [Missing data: bounded FIML](model-fiml.html) for its limits.

Both are the same engine; only the objective changes, and so do the estimates.

A separate argument, `estimator = "MLR"`, leaves the estimates alone and changes the standard errors (sandwich) and
the model test (Yuan-Bentler scaled chi-square); see [the sem engine page](model-sem.html#mlr).

## Optimizer

The optimizer is the algorithm that finds the minimum of the estimator's
objective. `sem_control()` sets it for a listwise fit:

```{r}
#| label: sem-control
ctl <- sem_control(n_starts = 3, nloptr = list(maxeval = 20000L))
fit <- fit_sem(syntax, mediation_demo, control = ctl)
str(fit@diagnostics$protocol)
```

`optimizer = "auto"` (default) runs SLSQP for a listwise fit. A plain list
passed as `control` still means `nloptr` options. Bounded FIML runs a fixed
protocol, SLSQP and `nlminb` from three starts each, and the two must agree;
only `optimizer = "auto"` is accepted there. Every fit records the protocol
that ran in `fit@diagnostics$protocol`.

A different optimizer does not change what is estimated. When the search fails,
the fit stops with an error or reports an unresolved result; it does not return
a different answer.

## The four layers

| Layer | Question | Examples | Does swapping it change the meaning of the result? |
|---|---|---|---|
| Engine | which fitter, hence which models and effects exist | `glm`, `regmedint`, `lmer`, `sem` | yes |
| Estimator | what is minimized | OLS, REML, listwise ML, bounded FIML | yes |
| Optimizer | which algorithm finds the minimum | SLSQP, `nlminb` | no: same objective; a failure is an error or an unresolved result |
| Inference | how uncertainty is computed | delta method, sandwich, bootstrap, MBCO | the interval, not the estimate |

Inference is covered in [Which interval should I use?](guide-intervals.html).

`compare_lr(engine = )` uses the word in another sense: there it names the
outside program, lavaan or OpenMx, that refits the model for the comparison.
It is not a fitter of the mediation model.
